contract:
FOLD THIS SIGNAL (plain text, no em-dashes, under 150 words): the row below is a signal an estate captured. Answer three things only: (1) TRUE-TODAY: is this signal still true given everything else you know in the row's context - yes/no/unknown with one line of why; (2) THE ORGAN: which kind of organ should own this signal (a law, a clock, a gate, a memory row, or compost); (3) THE FALSIFIER: the observation that would prove the signal wrong. Mark unknowns UNKNOWN; do not pad.

SIGNAL: CONTEXT: Operator runs bare-metal infrastructure with data in a Merkle/Verkle commitment tree. Root R is published externally. Neutral party requests proof for key k. Operator returns compact proof π. Verifier recomputes from π alone and checks against independently-obtained R. ROLE: Cryptographic protocol designer — specify a concrete, buildable mechanism for compact tree proofs that are verifiable against a public root without trusting the operator. TASK: Specify the exact proof format, verification algorithm, and falsifiable test for a compact Merkle proof that works against own-iron infras
